# Product Brief

## Derived

Facts grounded in this repository. Every line cites at least one path.

- **What it is:** A personal library of 49 Claude Code skills — markdown prompt packages the harness loads on demand — of which `product-review` is one, a panel-based reviewer that reads a diff through selected role profiles (`product-review/skill.md`, repository root listing).
- **Users and tenancy:** Single author, no accounts, no auth, no tenancy of any kind; the consumers are the author and the Claude Code harness itself, which invokes skills by name (no auth or user model anywhere in the tree; `product-review/skill.md` frontmatter).
- **Business model:** None. No billing, payment, subscription, plan, quota, or entitlement code exists anywhere in the repository (no billing dependencies, no plan configuration, no metering).
- **Surfaces:** Markdown skill definitions read by the harness; one shell script, `product-review/log.sh`, requiring bash and `python3`; JSON run logs under `product-review/logs/`. No web app, no HTTP API, no packaged CLI, no integrations.
- **Sensitive data:** The product itself collects no personal data. Run logs (`product-review/logs/*.json`, ~60 KB across six dated files) store verbatim questions, findings, and code excerpts from whatever repository was reviewed, which may be proprietary; `.gitignore` excludes `**/logs/*` and `**/config.json` from version control.
- **Delivery:** No CI, no build step, no test suite, no release process — edits take effect the moment they are saved, and git is the only versioning mechanism (`.gitignore`; no `.github/` directory).
- **Maturity signals:** `product-review` carries 29 registered role profiles plus a `_template.md` (`product-review/role-profiles/`), totalling roughly 29,000 words against ~3,000 words in `skill.md`; logging is on by default (`product-review/config.json`) and six days of runs have accumulated with no step that reads them back.

## Inferred

Model knowledge, not observation. **Cannot support a finding.** Verify before repeating.

- **Category:** Agent skill library — reusable prompt packages that extend an AI coding assistant, authored as plain markdown with a frontmatter contract.
- **Conventional capabilities in this category:** A top-level README or index of available skills; per-skill usage examples; some form of versioning or changelog; an evaluation or regression harness that runs prompts against fixed inputs; install or sync instructions when skills are shared.
- **Likely competitive set:** Anthropic's own skill and plugin distribution channels, and public community skill collections. Claims to confirm, not established facts — this ecosystem moves faster than the model's knowledge of it.
- **Category direction:** Toward packaged, versioned, installable skills with declared dependencies, and toward evaluation harnesses that treat prompts as testable artefacts rather than prose.

> These claims reflect the model's knowledge at training time and decay quickly.
> Named-competitor claims are the least reliable and must be phrased as claims to
> confirm, never as established fact.

## Unknowns

Facts the code cannot reveal. Roles must not assume these — treat each as "unknown",
not as "absent". A human can fill these in; do not invent them.

- Whether these skills are intended for personal use only or for publication and distribution
- Which skills are actively used versus abandoned experiments
- How long run logs should be retained, and whether their captured code excerpts are acceptable to keep
- Any audience beyond the author, and what they would need in order to adopt a skill
- Roadmap and strategic direction for the library as a whole
